requirements.title: ASSOCIATED procedure TARGET cases compare procedure identity and host instance
requirements.definition: With a procedure TARGET, ASSOCIATED is true exactly when the procedure pointer is associated with the same effective procedure target, including the same live host instance for internal procedures; dummy procedure and procedure pointer TARGET cases use the ultimate argument or procedure pointer association described by the source and still require the same host instance for internal procedures.

pending.associated-procedure-target-same-procedu: Use two module procedures with the same interface and a procedure pointer assigned to one; assert ASSOCIATED is true for the assigned procedure and false for the other. Also use the recursive-host internal-procedure control from the host-instance facet so an internal procedure target is checked with the same live host instance before the different-instance false case.
pending.associated-procedure-target-same-host-in: Use a recursive host procedure with an internal procedure and matching procedure-pointer interface. In the outer invocation, assign p_outer to the internal procedure and recurse before the outer invocation returns; in the inner invocation, assign p_inner to that invocation's internal procedure. While both host instances are live, initialize logical sentinels oppositely and assert same-instance ASSOCIATED(p_inner, inner) is true, different-instance ASSOCIATED(p_outer, inner) is false for case (ii), the same true/false distinction holds when inner is passed as a non-pointer dummy procedure for case (iii), and ASSOCIATED(p_outer, p_inner) is false while two pointers to the current inner procedure are true for case (iv). No procedure pointer is used after its host instance returns.
pending.associated-dummy-procedure-ultimate-argu: Pass a module procedure through a dummy procedure argument and assert a procedure pointer associated with the ultimate argument yields true; repeat inside the recursive-host setup with the current internal procedure passed as the dummy so same-host-instance is true and the outer-instance pointer is false.
pending.associated-procedure-pointer-same-proced: Assign two procedure pointers to the same and then different module procedures and assert ASSOCIATED(pointer,target_pointer) true and false respectively; for internal procedures, use the recursive-host setup to assert two current-instance pointers are true and outer-vs-current live instances are false.

requirements.title: ASSOCIATED data TARGET cases compare nonzero storage, shape, and storage-unit overlap in array order
requirements.definition: With a scalar data TARGET, ASSOCIATED is true exactly when TARGET is not a zero-sized storage sequence and POINTER occupies the same storage units as TARGET. With an array data TARGET, ASSOCIATED is true exactly when POINTER has the same shape, the associated array is neither of size zero nor an array whose elements are zero-sized storage sequences, and the storage units are the same in array element order.

pending.associated-scalar-target-same-nonzero-st: Use a scalar TARGET integer associated with a scalar pointer and another distinct scalar target; assert true for the same nonzero-sized target and false for the distinct target after opposite sentinels.
pending.associated-array-target-same-shape: Associate a rank-one pointer with a nonzero full-array target, then compare against same-shape and different-shape nonzero array targets; assert only exact logical results.
pending.associated-array-target-nonzero-elements: Use a nonzero-size, nonzero-element-storage array as an associated true control, then use the zero-size and zero-length-element variants in the separate pending plans to require false results without default-value vacuity.
pending.associated-array-target-same-storage-arr: Use an array pointer associated with a nonzero full array and compare with the full array and a shifted nonzero section of the same shape; assert storage/order-sensitive true and false results.
pending.associated-scalar-target-not-zero-sized-: Use a deferred-length character pointer with character(len=1), TARGET :: nz and character(len=0), TARGET :: z. First associate the pointer with nz, initialize the observed logical to .false., and assert ASSOCIATED(pointer,nz) is true; then associate the pointer with z, initialize the observed logical to .true., and assert ASSOCIATED(pointer,z) is false because the scalar TARGET is a zero-sized storage sequence.
pending.associated-array-target-not-size-zero: Use a rank-one pointer and integer TARGET array arr(2). First associate the pointer with arr, initialize the observed logical to .false., and assert ASSOCIATED(pointer,arr) is true; then associate the pointer with the zero-size section arr(1:0), initialize the observed logical to .true., and assert ASSOCIATED(pointer,arr(1:0)) is false because the array has size zero.
pending.associated-array-target-elements-not-zer: Use a deferred-length character array pointer with character(len=1), TARGET :: nz(1) and character(len=0), TARGET :: z(1). First associate the pointer with nz, initialize the observed logical to .false., and assert ASSOCIATED(pointer,nz) is true; then associate the pointer with z, initialize the observed logical to .true., and assert ASSOCIATED(pointer,z) is false because the array elements are zero-sized storage sequences even though the array size is one.

requirements.title: ASSOCIATED pointer TARGET cases compare association, nonzero storage, shape, and storage units
requirements.definition: With a scalar pointer TARGET, ASSOCIATED is true exactly when POINTER and TARGET are both associated, their targets are not zero-sized storage sequences, and they occupy the same storage units. With an array pointer TARGET, ASSOCIATED is true exactly when both pointers are associated, have the same shape, are neither of size zero nor arrays whose elements are zero-sized storage sequences, and occupy the same storage units in array element order.

pending.associated-scalar-pointer-target-both-as: Use two scalar pointers, first with one disassociated and then both associated to the same target, and assert false then true with opposite logical sentinels.
pending.associated-scalar-pointer-target-same-no: Associate two scalar pointers to the same nonzero-size target and to distinct nonzero-size targets; assert true and false respectively.
pending.associated-array-pointer-target-both-ass: Use array pointers with one disassociated and then both associated; assert the required false and true states.
pending.associated-array-pointer-target-same-sha: Associate array pointers to a nonzero full array and to a conforming remapped pointer target with distinguishable nonzero shape while preserving valid pointer association; assert same-shape true and different-shape false without relying on descriptor representation.
pending.associated-array-pointer-target-same-sto: Use full-array and shifted-section nonzero array pointers with equal shape but different storage start/order; assert ASSOCIATED distinguishes same storage units in array element order.
pending.associated-scalar-pointer-target-not-zer: Use two deferred-length character pointers with character(len=1), TARGET :: nz and character(len=0), TARGET :: z. First associate both pointers with nz, initialize the observed logical to .false., and assert ASSOCIATED(p1,p2) is true; then associate both pointers with z, initialize the observed logical to .true., and assert ASSOCIATED(p1,p2) is false because the scalar pointer targets are zero-sized storage sequences.
pending.associated-array-pointer-target-not-size: Use two rank-one integer pointers and TARGET array arr(2). First associate both pointers with arr, initialize the observed logical to .false., and assert ASSOCIATED(p1,p2) is true; then associate both pointers with the zero-size section arr(1:0), initialize the observed logical to .true., and assert ASSOCIATED(p1,p2) is false because the array pointer targets have size zero.
pending.associated-array-pointer-target-elements: Use two deferred-length character array pointers with character(len=1), TARGET :: nz(1) and character(len=0), TARGET :: z(1). First associate both pointers with nz, initialize the observed logical to .false., and assert ASSOCIATED(p1,p2) is true; then associate both pointers with z, initialize the observed logical to .true., and assert ASSOCIATED(p1,p2) is false because the associated arrays have zero-sized storage-sequence elements.
